facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and complete separation of the stratum corneum are characteristic of peeling skin syndrome.

The patient's skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and lesions predominantly located at areas of friction, along with the genetic mutations in the CDSN gene, are characteristic of acral peeling skin syndrome.
The patient's skin fragility, superficial skin erosions, and complete separation of the stratum corneum are characteristic of keratolysis exfoliativa congenita.

The presence of superficial skin erosions with unusual linear geographic contours, negative serological markers for celiac disease, and normal immunofluorescence mapping results for collagen and laminin explain the uncovered facts.

rationales.F01: Skin fragility is a key feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F05: Unusual linear geographic contour of lesions is characteristic of peeling skin syndrome and acral peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F09: Complete separation of the stratum corneum is a distinctive feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F10: Clean split just above the stratum granulosum is a characteristic finding in peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F11: Heterozygous mutations in the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome type B.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of skin fragility since early infancy, mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions, and erythematous residual macules from previous erosions are well-explained by Peeling skin syndrome, and the absence of admitted_against findings supports this diagnosis.
